newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein steady, eyes on rupiah.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein steady, eyes on rupiah.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices held steady in late trading on Monday, with demand staying moderate and players keeping watch on the rupiah, traders said.
They said palm olein was quoted at 1,650-60 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening but significantly higher than last Friday's close of 1,570 rupiah.
"Demand was moderate, and most players were keeping watch on the rupiah because any further declines against the U.S. dollar will mean an upward adjustment," one trader said.

"This is because local prices have to adjust to export prices, which are very good," one trader said. "If local prices are not comparable to export prices, players will prefer to export their oil than sell in the local market."
The traders said the surge in palm olein prices had spooked buyers, who were only buying for their immediate needs.
"They are only buying what they need immediately. They are not buying to replenish stocks because of the high prices," one trader said. "They are also waiting to see price developments."
The rupiah remained weak against the U.S. dollar and was quoted at 2,980/2,990 to the dollar at 0925 GMT, compared with 2,955-2,975 at 0345 GMT.

The traders also said there had been no signs of market intervention by state logistics agency BULOG, which sells palm olein at a discount directly to consumers when it feels that prices were beyond levels it considered reasonable.
"Players are watching to see if BULOG will enter the market, but as of now there has been nothing," one trader said.
